space.intro.sendsAndFinds: Send your captures and your night logs to your space, then find them on the web and on your other devices.
space.intro.names: PlanAstro is the app. Astro Portal is the portal, either the hosted service or the open-source server, where your space lives (the “Astro Portal space”). Astro Sync is this desktop companion that processes and sends your captures, and analyzes your nights.
space.intro.withoutSpaceShort: Without a space, Astro Sync can neither list your sessions nor send them.
space.email.helpShort: We send you a six-digit code.
space.email.helpMore: If this address has no space yet, one is created. This computer will be attached to your space.

settings.title: Settings

settings.folder.line: Astro Sync creates one folder per night in it; it never touches your own files. Its processing files are cleaned below.

settings.processing.title: Processing files
settings.processing.line: What Astro Sync makes in your working folder to stack and analyse your nights. Your own files are never touched there.
settings.processing.details: Astro Sync never touches your own files: frames, calibration, logs, final images, whether copied, moved or linked into the folder. Only its own processing files are cleaned here, and it makes them again at the next treatment that needs them. A link is never followed: its target, your frame, stays where it is.

settings.polished.title: Engine of the polished render

guide.title: Guide
guide.lead: How Astro Sync arranges a night, and how to help it.
guide.structure.lead: One folder per night in your working folder; folder names stay in English.
guide.table.use: What Astro Sync does with it
guide.row.logs.contents: The night’s NINA, PHD2, ASIAIR logs.
guide.row.logs.use: Read: steps, guiding. The raw logs stay here; only the report may leave.
guide.row.calibration.contents: The calibration frames, by type; the flats by filter if you wish.
guide.row.calibration.use: Read for the checks and the progression. They never leave this computer.
guide.row.lights.contents: This target’s FITS frames, of one or several filters.
guide.row.lights.use: Read: headers, quality, stacking. They never leave this computer.
guide.row.final.contents: The processed final image: TIFF, JPEG or PNG.
guide.row.final.use: Sent: it is the target’s capture (or its variant).
guide.note.name: A night’s name: the date, the plan or the place, a short identifier. You can rename it: a hidden file keeps its identity.
guide.note.minimum: The minimum for a capture: an image in final/ (or the stack of the frames, with Advanced Sync+). The rest serves the measures, the progression and the checks.
guide.note.results: Only results are sent: the final or stacked image, the report of the logs, the sky solutions, the progression images. The FITS frames and the raw logs never leave this computer.
guide.note.never: Astro Sync creates the folders; it never touches your own files: it never moves, renames or deletes them. Its processing files are cleaned in Settings.
guide.note.band: When the frames carry no FILTER, Astro Sync reads the band in the names: put it in the night’s folder name (180s_dualband, RGB, UVIR_cut) or in the first heading of a SESSION.md beside the frames. It only preselects the band; you can change it. Only broadband and dual-band are told apart for now.

guide.finder.captured: Finder · macOS, on a demonstration folder
guide.finder.alt: Screenshot of the Finder: the working folder, a night, its targets and the frames of M31.

guide.finder.finalLine: Drag the export of your processing software into M31/final/: full-resolution TIFF, JPEG or PNG.
guide.finder.hiddenLine: Each night and each target have a file whose name starts with a dot: leave it, it keeps their identity.
guide.move.line: A night weighs tens of GB: on the same disk, moving is instant and does not double the space used. In the Finder, ⌘ while dragging also moves to another disk.

guide.links.line: To leave the frames on an external disk: a link in place of the lights/ folder. Astro Sync follows the link and says so when the disk is missing.
guide.nina.line: So that NINA writes straight into the night: Options › Imaging, then these two settings. Flats taken in the same sequence will be flagged, to be moved.

wizard.treatments.integration.title: The night’s integration
wizard.treatments.integration.line: Integrates the frames of lights/ of each ticked target, family by family (filter, exposure, gain, binning, temperature). One line per family goes to your space, never a file.
master.entry.title: Measure a master
master.entry.line: Did you stack in PixInsight, Siril or another program? Astro Sync measures the quality of the image (width and roundness of the stars) on your master, as it does for its own stacking.
master.title: Measure a master
master.give: Give the linear master, as it comes out of the stacking, before any stretch or processing (FITS or XISF). A stretched image or a JPEG cannot be measured.
master.lead: Only the figures of the measure leave with the image; the file stays on this computer.
master.pending.measure: The master {file} will be measured when you continue.
master.pending.skipped: The master {file} will not be measured.
master.pending.forget: The measure kept will be removed when you continue.
master.refusal.stretched: Stretched image: measure the linear master, as it comes out of the stacking, before any stretch or processing (FITS or XISF). The stars of a stretched image are wider than the data they came from.
master.refusal.too_few_stars: Fewer than twenty isolated, measurable stars were found in this image: nothing is measured. Check that this is the master of the stacking.
master.refusal.unsupported_format: This file is neither a FITS nor an XISF. Give the linear master of the stacking (FITS or XISF); a JPEG or a TIFF cannot be measured.
master.refusal.unreadable: This file could not be read: it is damaged, or compressed in a way Astro Sync does not read (XISF uncompressed or compressed with zlib or LZ4 is read, zstd is not).
master.refusal.not_an_image: This file holds no measurable image: a two-dimensional image, in grey levels or with three channels, is expected.
master.refusal.reserved: Measuring a master is reserved to Advanced Sync+.
master.refusal.python_missing: Astro Sync’s Python environment is not installed: install it in Settings › Dependencies.
master.refusal.night_missing: The folder of this target cannot be found in the night’s folder.
deviceMaster.title: Image stacked by the device
deviceMaster.formatSolved: Linear RGB, 16-bit · field solution in the header
deviceMaster.splitWhy: The device cut this family into {images} images ({counts}): none holds all {total}. Astro Sync does not combine two device images: a new stacking of the frames is proposed for this family.
deviceMaster.splitBiggest: The device cut this family into {images} images ({counts}) and the frames are not on this computer: Astro Sync proposes the biggest, which leaves {aside} aside.
deviceMaster.line: Astro Sync can take it as the master of the target instead of a new stacking: you choose at the “Processing” step, where it is proposed by default.
deviceMaster.jpgNever: The .jpg of the same name, stretched, is never taken for a master.
deviceMaster.familiesApart: Different families of frames ({families}) never mix: each has its own image and its own choice, at the “Processing” step.
deviceMaster.jpg.withPoses: This image is a .jpg: stretched (and the device may have denoised it), it can be neither a master nor the start of a render. Astro Sync stacks the frames of lights/, as before.
deviceMaster.jpg.copyFit: To use the device’s image, copy its .fit file too (same name).
deviceMaster.jpg.alone: No frames and no .fit file: only this .jpg is left. Astro Sync makes neither a master nor a render of it.
deviceMaster.jpg.final: Put in final/, it can leave as it is as a final image (sending the final image already processed). Otherwise, copy the .fit and the device’s frames.
deviceMaster.ready: ready at once: no wait, no disk space.
deviceMaster.useWhy: {images} images ({counts}): none holds all {total} of the family.
deviceMaster.noPoses: The frames are not on this computer.
deviceMaster.restackDetail: The {poses} of lights/ · about {duration} and {space} of free space while it works.
deviceMaster.restackUseful: Useful for several nights, a night cut into several images, bad frames to leave out, finer stars.
deviceMaster.pipelinesNote: The pipelines chosen start from it as from an Astro Sync stacking: stretch, stars, contrast.
deviceMaster.unused: Not applicable to the device’s image, already stacked: the measure of the frames, “Leave out the flagged frames”, calibration (darks, flats). They come back if you stack again.
deviceMaster.pending: This image will be measured when you continue.
deviceMaster.measuredOn: Measured on {file}, a linear image. These figures leave with the images of {target}; the file stays on this computer.
deviceMaster.why.nights.title: Several nights to combine.
deviceMaster.why.nights.text: The device stacks each night on its own; for the image of a multi-night plan, Astro Sync starts again from the frames of each night.
deviceMaster.why.cut.title: A night cut into several images.
deviceMaster.why.cut.text: When the device cuts a family of frames into several images, stacking the frames again makes only one.
deviceMaster.why.cut.night: On {day}, the {poses} are in {images} images of the device ({counts}); stacked again, they make one image of {total}.
deviceMaster.why.missed.title: Bad frames to leave out.
deviceMaster.why.missed.text: The device stacks every frame, the ones at dawn included; the measure of the frames flags the worst, you leave them out, and the stacking skips them.
deviceMaster.why.finer.title: Finer stars.
deviceMaster.why.finer.text: On a night of M45 measured by Astro Sync: {percent}% finer than the device’s, with the same signal to noise ratio within ±5%.
deviceMaster.why.rows.snr: Signal to noise ratio of the stars
deviceMaster.why.caption: Measured example: M45, night of 10 to 11 October, 430 frames of 30 s, with Astro Sync’s own code. Nothing is deleted: the device’s image stays in its folder.
deviceMaster.why.footnote: The measure of the frames (“Files” step) and “Leave out the flagged frames” are available when you stack again.

multiNight.framing.beyondAny: Beyond the mark, the degradation grows: more of the image has less exposure.

detect.title: Detect sessions
detect.lead: Astro Sync reads the headers of your FITS files, finds the nights, targets, places and equipment, attaches the calibrations and logs to the nights, then shows you what it would create. Nothing is created without your approval.
detect.readOnly: Read-only: nothing in these folders is changed, moved or copied.
detect.readOnlyDetails: Astro Sync reads the headers (DATE-OBS, EXPTIME, IMAGETYP, OBJECT, coordinates, FILTER, SITELAT / SITELONG, TELESCOP, INSTRUME, FOCALLEN, GAIN, CCD-TEMP), limits plate solving to the frames without coordinates (one per group) and reads the logs with Astro Sync’s own readers (N.I.N.A., ASIAIR, PHD2).

fileMode.windowsNoLink: On Windows, a symbolic link needs developer mode.
organise.moveLine: Each file is copied, checked by its fingerprint (SHA-256), and only then deleted from the source. If a check fails, that file is not deleted and you will find it in the final list.
organise.copyLine: Copy of {count} files. The originals are not touched.
organise.linkLine: The files stay in {path}; each night’s folder points to them. This folder must stay reachable for sending, stacking and checks.
organise.leaveLine: The files stay where they are, as today. You can tidy them later from each session.
organise.progressNote: Nothing is deleted from the source before each file is checked.

detect.review.details: Each ticked line is created at the Summary, when you press “Create and send” (or “Create”). Until then nothing is written to your space: the treatments work in provisional folders of your working folder. The sessions created are “Executed”, with a one-night plan rebuilt from the frames, and carry “Imported by Astro Sync”. Your files are not modified, moved or sent.
